newsitem.title: USA: Financial reform details up to Congress -- Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Financial reform details up to Congress -- Greenspan.

text.p: The specifics of what types of mergers should be allowed under financial reform proposals should be up to Congress, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said Wednesday.
"Congress has to make the judgment as to what degree of merging of commerce and banking occurs," Greenspan said in testimony to a House Banking subcommittee.

The Fed chief said the central bank could look at the implications of a reform proposal on the overall structure of the financial system but said it was not its role to determine "qualitative" issues, such as the size of institutions that could be acquired.
"What we cannot do -- and I don't think it's appropriate for us to be involved with -- is to make these very fundamental judgments as to the balance of powers within this nation," Greenspan said.
